title: Compact workspace rail with choreographed switcher and route compression
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The current left rail in Redwood Console is verbose for users who juggle multiple workspaces and routes (dashboards, rollouts, cost views). Dense menus lead to slow context switches and visual noise. Goal: Design a compact, multi-layer rail that supports rapid workspace switching, surface-level route compression (grouping related routes into micro-lenses), and a choreographed switcher animation that preserves spatial context and minimizes cognitive load.

Scope:
- UX patterns for a 'compact rail' that expands contextually on hover/focus and pins on demand.
- New micro-lens taxonomy to group routes (e.g., Observability: latency/cost/alerts; Deployments: rollouts/canary/history).
- Workspace switcher mini-map: an in-rail preview that shows recent routes per workspace without full navigation.
- Interaction choreography: motion spec for switcher transitions to retain user mental model.
- Accessibility and keyboard/ARIA behavior for compressed routes and workspace cycling.

Non-goals:
- Major backend routing changes. The design must be implementable via existing Console routes and feature flags.

Success metrics:
- 20% reduction in average time-to-open target route in usability test tasks.
- 15% lift in successful route discovery for first-time power users.
- Zero regression on keyboard-only navigation (measured by accessibility smoke tests).

Constraints:
- Must work within current layout grid (max width of compact rail = 72px).
- Must be compatible with dedicated and private console feature toggles.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Jonas Petrov (product lead for console), Eng lead: Priya Raman (frontend), OBS lead: Gabriel Ortiz, Security: Lila Singh.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype (compact rail master + 3 flow variants: hovering, pinned, workspace-mini-map).
- Motion spec (duration/easing and reduced-motion variants).
- Accessibility spec: ARIA roles, keyboard map, focus order.
- Implementation handoff doc with route grouping map and analytics events.

Rollout plan:
- Canary behind feature flag for 10% of console users (opt-in in workspace settings).
- Telemetry events to measure route selection, switcher open/close, and pin toggles.
- Phased expansion after two-week observation window and bug fixes.

Implementation notes for eng:
- Frontend should reuse existing route IDs; grouping is purely presentation-layer (no new server routes).
- Use CSS variables for rail widths and reduced-motion media query.

Attachments: ["https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/compact-chorus-rail-proto-2026", "https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CON/Compact+Rail+IA+Spec", "https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4821 (placeholder for implementation PR)"]
comments: 2026-02-10 — Ava Martinez: Initial kickoff. Mapped current pain points from support tickets and session replays. Proposed micro-lens taxonomy draft attached to Figma. Asked Eng to validate feasible DOM affordances for hover expansion.

2026-02-12 — Priya Raman (eng): Feasibility note — hover expansion via CSS transforms is fine; need to avoid layout shift on mobile. Prefers pointer-based hover only, with click-to-expand on touch. Recommends animation duration <= 180ms for snappy feel.
2026-02-14 — Jonas Petrov (PM): Prioritized this as high-impact for power-user flows (dashboards & rollouts). Requested telemetry plan with event names. Suggested making pin state workspace-scoped.

2026-02-18 — Design review: Team reviewed three layout variants (icon-only, stacked micro-lenses, stacked + mini preview). Decision: move forward with icon + micro-lens grouping and optional workspace-mini-map on hover for power users.

2026-02-22 — Usability prototype 1: Remote moderated tests with 8 participants (mix of new and power users). Findings: micro-lenses improved discoverability for Rollouts and Cost views; mini-map was confusing without clear affordance — will test a simplified preview with a visible chevron.

2026-02-25 — Accessibility pass: Confirmed keyboard navigation across compressed groups via arrow keys and Enter opens primary route. Need to add clear ARIA labels for compressed group toggles. Reduced-motion variant included.

2026-02-27 — Engineering sync: Agreed on analytics event schema: console.rail.open, console.rail.group_open, console.switcher.workspace_preview, console.rail.pin_toggle. Eng to instrument events in canary PR.

2026-03-01 — Design handoff: Finalized Figma screens and motion spec. Created Handoff doc in Confluence and recorded a 20-minute walkthrough for Eng. Next: ship canary behind flag and collect telemetry for two weeks.
2026-03-01 — Maya Chen (assignee): Picking up implementation. Will create ENG-11022 for frontend work and ENG-11023 for telemetry. Planning spike to validate keyboard focus trap interactions (2d).
